subject: BrightShore: sudden long-tail latency & request fan-out causing queue lock

Date: Tue, 1 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Latency spike affecting BrightShore checkout - urgent

Hi Irene,

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95/p99 latency on our checkout flows around 03:30 UTC today. Symptoms:
- P99 jumped from ~420ms to >2.8s for several 10-minute windows.
- Intermittent 502/503 errors for personalization endpoints.
- Overall throughput to your API fell ~30% despite steady inbound traffic.

Our engineering team captured traces and a small sampling of request headers (attached: brightshore_trace_0501.zip). The pattern looks like a request fan-out from our side into long-running hatched flows in your pipeline that then appear to backpressure other requests (queueing and stalls).

This is impacting a subset of high-value checkouts. Can you confirm whether you see increased queue depth / backpressure in the last 4 hours? We need an ETA on mitigation — customer experience is degraded and we may escalate internally if this isn't resolved in the hour.

Thanks,
Alice Nguyen
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightShore

Thanks Alice — we see the alerts and have started triage. Preliminary signal from our telemetry: sudden increase in queue_length and a small but sustained rise in concurrency caps tripping on a subset of backend pools (pool-3 / policy=reserved).

Plan (first 60 minutes):
- Triage call in 10m to correlate traces (joining: karthik, Ben, Lauren).
- Temporarily raise concurrency cap on pool-3 (manual increase) to relieve immediate tail latencies.
- Enable per-customer request prioritization for BrightShore traffic to reduce fan-out impact on other flows.
- Collect targeted telemetry (kv-cache hit/miss, in-flight requests, queue depth) for next 30 mins.

We will keep you updated on progress and confirm when we see p99s falling back to baseline.

Subject: Re: Latency spike affecting BrightShore checkout - urgent

Quick telemetry note from infra:
- pool-3 serving BrightShore has a sudden pattern of long tail where requests with large context lengths are saturating the single-tenant execution lanes. KV cache eviction rate spiked ~09:28 UTC.
- Concurrency cap configured at 48 for that pool; we've observed transient bursts up to 120 concurrent tasks due to customer fan-out. The runtime's admission controller is tripping and queuing extra work, which pushes p99 up.

Immediate actions I recommend (we started executing):
1) Bump concurrency cap to 90 for pool-3 (temporary) and monitor queue drain.
2) Apply short-lived request-throttling token bucket for non-critical BrightShore routes to flatten fan-out.
3) Force fallback to lower-latency model variant for personalization where quality delta is acceptable.
4) Start an elevated trace collection for any request exceeding 1s.

Notes for post-mortem: evaluate batching policy and admission tuning for multi-tenant pools and consider a per-customer soft cap with emergency overrides.

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Forwarding the thread and current mitigation steps. TL;DR: BrightShore experienced a fan-out pattern that tripped concurrency admission on pool-3 and caused a queue lock (p99 >2s). We have:
- Increased concurrency cap on pool-3 from 48 -> 90 (temporary override).
- Enabled per-customer prioritization and throttling on a handful of non-critical routes.
- Rolled a lower-latency model variant for personalization requests (fallback).

Outstanding asks for leadership:
- Approve keeping temporary cap increase for up to 6 hours while we monitor (risk: cost bump).
- Approve manual emergency warm pool allocation if traffic re-spikes.
- Signal to Sales/AMs that we may need to apply a small credit if BrightShore reports continued impact.

Subject: Re: Latency spike affecting BrightShore checkout - urgent

Alice —

Thanks again for the heads up this morning. Quick summary of what we did and the outcome:
- Increased concurrency cap on pool-3 (48 -> 90) at 09:40; queue drained within ~18 minutes.
- Enabled per-customer prioritization and a short token-bucket throttle on non-critical personalization routes; this prevented fan-out from starving the shared pool.
- Rolled the lower-latency model variant for personalization traffic between 10:05–11:00 as an additional mitigation while we validated stability.

Post-mitigation numbers (10:00–12:00):
- P99 reduced from peak 2.8s -> 470ms.
- Error rate for affected endpoints returned to baseline.
- Throughput recovered to expected levels.

Attached is an incident brief (incident_summary_0501.pdf) with the timeline, telemetry snippets, and recommended follow-ups:
- Short-term: revert concurrency cap at 15:00 if stable, finalize a per-customer soft-cap policy.
- Medium-term: tune admission controller to be more aggressive on KV-cache pressure and add automatic emergency warm pool policy.

Can you confirm whether your checkout success metrics look back to normal? We can keep daily checks for 48 hours and schedule a post-mortem with your team to agree on longer-term mitigations.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
